newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Luxembourg makes back-up plan for extra EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Luxembourg makes back-up plan for extra EU summit.

text.p: Luxembourg, which takes over the European Union presidency in July, has made a plan for an extra meeting of EU leaders if they fail to agree on institutional reform at their Amsterdam summit in June.
"There are two possible dates, in July or October," Luxembourg government press officer Guy Schuller told Reuters.

He confirmed Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker told reporters on Friday, following the government's weekly cabinet meeting, the two dates being considered were July 25 and October 10/11. Luxembourg's traditonal end-of-presidency summit is due to be held on December 12 and 13.
Schuller said, however, this was contingency planning. "At the moment the odds are pretty good that there will be an agreement on the IGC (inter-governmental conference) at Amsterdam," he said.
Juncker told Reuters Financial Television in an interview broadcast on Monday that he hoped the Dutch Presidency, which began on January 1, would broker a deal on EU reform.
